edge: Produce an adjusted limit exactly zero and require the same clamp and warning.
notes: The diagnostic oracle is occurrence of a warning, not its wording.
positive: Produce an adjusted limit below zero and verify zero-limit behavior plus a warning.

edge: Exercise elapsed time exactly equal to the limit.
notes: Use each check's specific subclause for event derivation and comparison relation.
positive: Exercise elapsed times on each side of a check-specific limit.

edge: Hold upper bits opposite the LSB to prove they are ignored.
positive: Use scalar conditions and multibit values whose LSB controls enablement.

edge: Use one condition depending on both delayed reference and delayed data.
negative: Assume an ordinary condition signal is implicitly delayed with the checked signal.
positive: Form a condition from explicit delayed signals and use it as timestamp/timecheck condition.

edge: Apply x with ===, !==, negation, and bare expression and require no enablement.
notes: Source annotation warrants checking the visual source when materializing exact operator examples.
positive: Apply x with == and != conditions and require event enablement.

edge: Transition the signal while its condition is false, then true without another signal transition.
positive: Trigger an event while its condition is true.

edge: Choose values for which the original and adjusted limits produce opposite violation outcomes.
negative: Evaluate a listed check against the original unadjusted limit when a delayed signal requires adjustment.
positive: Exercise an explicit or implicit delayed signal with each listed timing check and verify evaluation uses the correspondingly adjusted limit.

edge: Set induced delay equal to the path delay and just above it.
positive: Use a negative limit whose induced delay exceeds a specify path delay and verify output follows the induced delay.

edge: Use exactly six distinct transition descriptors.
negative: Use an empty list or more than six descriptors.
positive: Use one and six descriptors.

edge: Compare x and z transition matching.
negative: Trigger an unlisted direction for a restricted edge list.
positive: Trigger each listed transition and corresponding z transition under its descriptor.

edge: Mix uppercase and lowercase forms in one edge list.
negative: Insert whitespace between descriptor characters.
positive: Use 01, 10, 0x, X1, z0, and 1Z descriptors.

edge: Exercise transitions to and from z under shorthand and explicit forms.
positive: Compare posedge against its three-descriptor form and negedge against its form over 0/1/x/z transitions.

edge: Mix explicit shared reference with implicit distinct data signals.
positive: Use one signal in two checks, explicitly naming its delayed copy in only one, and verify both use that copy.

edge: Provide the opposite event just before expiration and require no violation plus dormancy.
positive: Start windows with each event type and omit the opposite event to observe expiration violations.

edge: Provide a false-conditioned timestamp and require no activation except as governed by remain_active replacement rules.
positive: After dormancy, provide an unconditional timestamp and a true-conditioned timestamp.

edge: Deliver a timecheck exactly at the limit and just within it.
positive: Deliver a late timecheck and verify both violation and immediate start of the opposite-direction window.

edge: Swap events one simulation precision unit apart to isolate each event-order mapping.
positive: Exercise reference-first and data-first sequences and verify the corresponding timestamp/timecheck mapping.

edge: Use zero and unequal directional limits.
negative: Use a negative limit or runtime-varying flag.
positive: Use distinct limits in each event order and all flag combinations.

edge: Issue a false-conditioned second timestamp with remain_active set and clear.
positive: Issue a second valid timestamp before completion and verify the window restarts.

edge: Use equality, simultaneous events with zero limit, and replacement timestamp at expiration.
positive: Exceed each directional limit in its corresponding event order.

edge: Place data at the ending endpoint and use a zero limit; require no violation.
negative: Use a negative or nonconstant hold limit.
positive: Place a data event at the timestamp or strictly inside a positive hold window and require a violation.

edge: Use differing negative limits across checks sharing the reference.
notes: Observation may require behavior that distinguishes duplicated from shared delayed state.
positive: Use one reference signal in two negative checks and distinct data signals; require one logical delayed copy per distinct source signal.

edge: Construct a case requiring multiple limits to be changed to zero.
notes: Smallest means the most negative numeric limit in the source wording.
positive: Provide mutually inconsistent negative limits and verify warning plus iterative normalization.

edge: Combine three or more condition inputs into one scalar signal outside the specify block.
negative: Attempt to define the combining logic inside the specify block.
positive: Combine two conditions in module logic and use the resulting scalar in &&&.

edge: Place the two delayed transitions one simulation precision unit apart and swap their order.
positive: Construct one case where delayed reference transitions first and one where delayed data transitions first, using distinguishable conditions.

edge: Declare only the delayed signals needed by the production's optional positions.
negative: Attempt to reference an implicitly created delayed signal.
positive: Declare delayed signals and reference them in model logic; separately omit them with a negative limit and verify check evaluation.

edge: Use unequal data and reference delays around the reference edge.
positive: Use negative setup or hold and verify violation timing against the shifted window.

edge: Use one negative and one positive limit satisfying the required sum.
notes: Materialization requires a standardized or harness-supported way to enable the language option.
positive: Under negative-check mode, apply equivalent negative-limit scenarios to setuphold and recrem and compare behavior.

edge: Place transitions at boundaries according to the detailed negative-check rules.
positive: Place a data transition inside the shifted negative-limit window and require a violation.

edge: Choose values where adjusted and original violation times coincide as a control.

edge: Toggle source signals multiple times in one time unit and verify copy behavior.

positive: Run a model with declared delayed signals with negative mode disabled and with all checks disabled; compare each copy to its original.

edge: Transition data exactly at each endpoint.

positive: Arrange one value stable throughout the open window and verify that value is latched.

edge: Change at each endpoint and use a window narrower than two precision units; require no violation.
positive: Change data strictly inside a window at least two precision units wide.

edge: Use constant mintypmax expressions for both offsets.

positive: Use constant positive, zero, and negative offsets.

edge: Place data at each endpoint and require no violation; use zero offsets.
